      <title>Threat of AI share crash puts world financial stability at risk, says IMF</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/13/ai-share-crash-risk-global-imf-debt-corrowing-cyber-attacks</link>
      <description><p>High valuations and debt put sector in danger, while fund also warns on government borrowing and cyber-attacks</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/13/imf-global-economy-world-economic-outlook-uk-gdp-forecast-2026">IMF warns global economy ‘could soon test the limits of resilience’</a></p></li></ul><p>The threat of an AI share price crash rippling out across global markets is putting world financial stability at risk, the International Monetary fund has warned.</p><p>In its twice-yearly Global Financial Stability Report, the IMF highlighted the sky-high valuations for AI companies along with their increasing debt pile as one reason that risks in the system are “elevated”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/13/ai-share-crash-risk-global-imf-debt-corrowing-cyber-attacks">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Martin Shkreli’s 2022 release conditions bar him from participating in the pharmaceutical industry, including ownership stakes or business decisions</p><p>The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and seven US states have alleged that pharmaceutical executive Martin Shkreli repeatedly violated a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/jan/14/martin-shkreli-barred-drug-industry-fined-us-court">lifetime ban</a> on participating in the pharmaceutical industry, and they are asking a judge to hold him in contempt.</p><p>In a <a href="https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/10/ftc-states-ask-federal-court-hold-martin-shkreli-contempt-allegedly-violating-lifetime">motion </a>filed on Tuesday in US district court in New York City, the FTC and its state co-plaintiffs allege that 43-year-old Shkreli – nicknamed the “Pharma Bro” – has traded stocks in at least 60 pharmaceutical companies and publicly commented on their businesses since his release from prison in May 2022.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/13/martin-shkreli-ftc-ruling-pharma-ban">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>US economists developed models that help central bankers and finance ministers to stabilise their economies</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/oct/12/uk-growth-inflation-pressures-oil-price-sveriges-riksbank-nobel-prize-economic-sciences-awarded-latest-news-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Two US economists have won the 2026 Nobel economics prize for their work developing models that help central bankers and finance ministers to stabilise their countries, avoiding long recessions and runaway inflation.</p><p>Robert Hall of Stanford University, California, and Michael Woodford of Columbia University, New York, were recognised for <a href="https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2026/10/advanced-economicsciencesprize2026.pdf">developing the “microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation”</a>, giving policymakers better tools to smooth out the peaks and troughs of their economies.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/12/nobel-prize-for-economics-hall-woodford-new-keynesian-models">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The pre-midterm defenestration of ACA enrollees looks like political madness – but the president appears to believe hitting poor people might work for him</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/08/economy-midterm-elections-tell-us">Send us your questions on how the US economy is shaping the midterm elections</a></p></li></ul><p>There is a manic quality to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s desperate dash to do something, anything, ahead of November’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-midterm-elections-2026">midterm elections</a> to convince beleaguered Americans that he can make the pressures his policies have imposed on their livelihoods go away.</p><p>The US president <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/28/trump-cattle-ranchers-beef-imports-backlash">offered</a> to lower barriers against beef imports to limit surging meat prices, only to consider <a href="https://www.politico.com/news/2026/09/23/trump-beef-imports-midterms-gop-panic-01090261">backtracking</a> under <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/25/trump-republican-backlash-beef-tariff-import">pressure</a> from the cow lobby. He weakened fuel efficiency standards, claiming this would trim the price of a new car (and forgetting to point out it will also raise spending on gas). In early October he started mailing <a href="https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/01/economy/trump-obamacare-500-check">$500 checks</a> to nearly a million people touting his healthcare “wins”. Oh, and he promised adult Americans a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/10/trump-5000-midterm-cash-dividend-response">$5,000 check</a> if Republicans maintain control of Congress.
